title: Gail and the Cloud That Could Not Stop Thundering

en: A small wooden chest waits beside Gail’s bed.
She carefully lifts the lid and finds a brass bell tucked inside.
Gail lifts the bell and gives it a gentle shake.
A clear chime rings out, and silver mist rises around it, opening a way to a grassy hill.
On the hill, Gail meets a small cloud floating above the grass.
Below it lies a careful spiral of orange and green leaves.
A breeze slips through the trees and across the hill.
The edges of the leaf spiral begin to lift from the ground.
A stronger gust scatters the leaves across the grass.
Cloud watches the pattern it worked so hard to make come apart.
The loose leaves spin beyond Cloud’s reach.
The faster Cloud rushes after them, the harder it becomes to arrange anything.
Cloud grows darker, and a clap of thunder rolls across the hill.
Gail steps back and gives her new friend some space.
Another loud rumble follows the first.
Gail stays nearby without shouting over it, waiting until Cloud can hear her.
“I am angry!” Cloud says when the rumble fades.
Gail does not ask it to smile or pretend nothing happened.
“I am upset because my work blew away,” Cloud explains.
Gail sits down to hear what the pattern meant to her friend.
Gail helps Cloud name the feelings without judging them.
“Angry about the wind, and upset about my work,” Cloud says.
Gail suggests a short pause before they do anything else.
They let the leaves rest where they landed and stop trying to chase every one.
Gail takes an easy breath in and slowly lets it out.
Cloud tries with her, making a little puff that turns the pinwheel.
They watch the pinwheel make a slow turn, then rest.
There is no race to feel better; they can take another easy breath when they are ready.
The rumble eases, and Cloud has a calm moment.
It still cares about the broken pattern, but now it has room to choose what to do.
Cloud tells Gail what it needs instead of trying to manage alone.
“Please stay and help me begin again,” it asks.
Together, they begin again with the leaves that landed nearby.
The new spiral does not have to match the old one exactly.
Cloud tries a gentle breeze while Gail sets down the last leaf.
They choose a sheltered patch near the wall, so their new work can stay in place.
A soft shower settles the dust around their finished spiral.
Cloud knows strong feelings may return, and it can pause, name them, and ask for help again.
Back in her familiar room, Gail sets the bell beside the chest.
Its quiet chime reminds her that a pause can make space for the next small choice.
